summary: Length of the longest run of consecutive integers (any order) in O(n).
mainInsight: Put all numbers in a set. Only start counting from a number x with x - 1 not in the set (a sequence start); then walk x, x+1, ... while present. Each number is visited at most twice overall, so the total is O(n).

promptVariants: Which structure and trick gives O(n) for the longest consecutive sequence?
How do you avoid recounting the same run?
options: A set, counting only from numbers whose predecessor is absent
A max-heap that pops all of the numbers in sorted order
Two pointers moving over the unsorted array of numbers
A stack that keeps track of the current streak of numbers
cards.answer: A set, counting only from numbers whose predecessor is absent
cards.explanation: Every run is counted once, from its smallest element.

incorrectOptionExplanations.A stack that keeps track of the current: A stack does not locate neighbours.

promptVariants: Why is the nested while loop still O(n)?
How many times is each number touched?
cards.answer: The inner walk only runs for numbers that start a sequence (x - 1 absent). Each element belongs to exactly one sequence, so it is walked at most once by that sequence's start and checked once in the outer loop, giving O(n) total.
cards.explanation: Without the start check it degrades to O(n^2).
Set construction plus one walk per sequence start.
